intent: Show a label-weight title inside a FieldContent that is not a label element.
typical_uses: The title above a description in a FieldContent, when the control is named another way

dont_use_when.situation: A caption that should name the control and act as its click target

invariants.text: FieldTitle renders a plain div with the label type style and no role: it associates with no control, so the control needs its own accessible name. Inside a Field carrying data-disabled="true" it is dimmed to the disabled opacity.

anti_patterns.dont: Let a FieldTitle be the only name a control has
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use FieldLabel with htmlFor, or give the control its own aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at the title's id

good.title: A title that also names the switch through aria-labelledby
good.code:
<Field orientation="horizontal">
  <FieldContent>
    <FieldTitle id="updates-title">Product updates</FieldTitle>
    <FieldDescription>Release notes and roadmap changes.</FieldDescription>
  </FieldContent>
  <Switch aria-labelledby="updates-title" />
</Field>

bad.title: A title pointed at by htmlFor
bad.why: FieldTitle is a div, not a label; htmlFor does nothing on it. Use FieldLabel when the caption should name the control.
